title: Free-float frames and the lattice of clocks
summary: Operational definition of inertial (free-float) frames; their local character and tidal limits; test particles; the latticework of rods and synchronised clocks; the observer as a lattice; measuring speed; the rocket frame.

objectives.description: Define and test an inertial frame using several free test particles and a stated tolerance.
Synchronise a stationary clock lattice and distinguish coordinate time from signal reception time.
Calculate moving-clock offsets and rates using explicit event pairs.
Estimate a tidal limit on the size and duration of a local inertial approximation.

preparation.description: Read Spacetime Physics Chapter 2 Floating Free (pp. 25–52): Sections 2.1–2.10 and the exercises.
Re-read Section 3.1 The Principle of Relativity (pp. 53–55).
Optional: MIT 8.20 Week 1 videos, Lecture 2.1 Events and Lecture 2.2 Galilean Transformation.

activities.title: Lecture notes and primary reading
activities.instructions: Work through the notes with the assigned source open. Reproduce each worked calculation or derivation on paper, including its assumptions, before reading the next step. Write one question that remains unresolved.

activities.title: Problem sheet: calculation, explanation and transfer
activities.instructions: Attempt the problems independently first. Use one hint at a time if useful, and record which help you used. Show the reasoning that connects the model and its assumptions to each answer; compare the reference only after a substantial attempt.

activities.title: Return without the notes
activities.instructions: On a later study day, close the notes and reconstruct the core relation and its assumptions, then explain the failure case from the last problem. Compare with your saved work and correct one gap. This practice does not itself certify mastery.

exitCheck.description: Use the whole problem sheet to judge the objectives: explain assumptions, complete the independent calculations and justify the final transfer/synthesis. The final exercise is the recorded checkpoint; its acceptance alone is not a claim that all course outcomes are mastered.

commonMisconceptions.claim: An observer is one person watching distant events.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The coordinate observer uses local synchronised clocks; received light needs a travel-time correction.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A freely falling laboratory is an exact inertial frame of any size.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Tidal relative acceleration limits the region and duration for a chosen accuracy.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Synchronised moving clocks must remain synchronised in every frame.
commonMisconceptions.correction: A change of simultaneity slice changes their displayed-time offset, although identical clocks retain equal rates within their own frame.
